clean.tx: He turu mai ia ki te hare hāpī koia ko te runurunu mai i te rāua tūava.
clean.tl: They went down to school, while picking (lit. with the picking) guavas.

clean.tx: Te haŋa era o Malo mo ai ko Hepu mo rē.
clean.tl: Malo wants (lit. ‘Malo’s wish’) Hepu to win.

clean.tx: Tāana kī: tae tātou hokotahi nō.
clean.tl: What she said, was: we are not alone.

clean.tx: Ka koa mai āpī e mai nehenehe a koe.
clean.tl: Be happy as long as you are young and beautiful.

clean.tx: I oti era he turu ki raro ki te teata mātaitai.
clean.tl: After that they went down to the theatre to watch.

clean.tx: Kai hauru mātou i aŋapō.
clean.tl: We did not sleep last night.

clean.tx: Te nuu ruku o aŋanīrā ko ai ana te raperape, te hio…

clean.tx: E vovo, anīrā he hoki māua ki uta.
clean.tl: My girl, today we will return to the field.

clean.tx: Āpō he ea tātou ki ruŋa ki te vaka.
clean.tl: Tomorrow we will go out by boat.

clean.tx: He ui atu a Eva ko te mee pē he tiare ā ka ī.
clean.tl: Eva saw something like flowers, in great numbers.

clean.tx: Pē he korohua era ko Iovani Itiiti te āriŋa.
clean.tl: His face (looks) like the old man Iovani Iti’iti.

clean.tx: Arero nei pa he arero rapa nui ā.
clean.tl: This language is like the Rapa Nui language.

clean.tx: Tae he aŋa ŋā vie rā.
clean.tl: That’s not women’s work.

clean.tx: Ka vānaŋa tahi rō i tou moe vārua.
clean.tl: Tell your dream completely.

clean.tx: E hakaheu ana tū rūau era i tāana kona oka tiare.
clean.tl: The old woman was weeding her flower garden.

clean.tx: A au i oho mai nei ki a koe mo noho ōoku i nei.
clean.tl: I have come to you to live here.

clean.tx: Ko koe i rē.
clean.tl: You have won.

clean.tx: ¡E Nuahine Pīkea Uri ē, āau rō taa moeŋa nei o māua i toke!
clean.tl: Nuahine Pikea Uri, it was you who stole that mat of ours!

clean.tx: He hakaroŋo mai tū taŋata era i tū vehi era.
clean.tl: The man listened to that song.

clean.tx: Poki era ko eke ā e te vārua.
clean.tl: The child is dominated/possessed by a spirit.

clean.tx: ¿E hia motu noho e te taŋata?
clean.tl: How many inhabited islands are there? (lit. How many islands lived by people)

clean.tx: E oo rō tōona hare e te tokerau.
clean.tl: Let his house be entered by the wind.

clean.tx: Mai tū hora era a Eva ina he taŋi hakaou.
clean.tl: From that moment on Eva did not cry again.

clean.tx: Āpō nō tāua ana vānaŋa.
clean.tl: Tomorrow we will talk.

clean.tx: O ira ko tū ŋā taina rikiriki nō era ōona te oho ki te hāpī.
clean.tl: Therefore only her little brothers went to school.

clean.tx: Te taŋata e mate tahi rō ā; ko koe nō, te ora te oho.
clean.tl: All people die, but you just keep on living.

clean.tx: He poreko te poki he nape ko Tikitiki a Ataraŋa.
clean.tl: The child was born, they called it Tikitiki a Ataranga.

clean.tx: He nape i te īŋoa ko Māhina Tea.
clean.tl: They called her (lit. her name) Mahina Tea.

clean.tx: He nape i te rāua īŋoa he hānau momoko.
clean.tl: They called them ‘slender race.

clean.tx: Ina a au e ko rehu i a koe.
clean.tl: You won’t forget me.

clean.tx: ¡I a au tau honu ena ana ŋaei!
clean.tl: By me that turtle will move! (=I will move that turtle)

clean.tx: A Tiki he poki o te raā e he atua rahi o rāua.
clean.tl: Tiki was the son of the sun and their high God.

clean.tx: A au he pūoko o Rapa Nui i te ao taatoa.
clean.tl: I am the head (leader) of Rapa Nui in the whole world.

clean.tx: ¿Ko ai te rūau era o tua ai?
clean.tl: Who is the old woman there in the back?

clean.tx: I oti era tū taŋata era i te vānaŋa…
clean.tl: When the man had finished speaking…

flagged.tl: (in the description of a house:) We are the only ones living here.
